title: What were the recorded values—not just the shape?
summary: Use Table to test a Graph hypothesis against selected samples and decoded events instead of relying on another visual impression.
questions: What value did this field have around the cursor?
Which controller and motor outputs surrounded the event?
Was a field recorded, derived, unavailable, or simply not selected?

blocks.text: Graphs are excellent at revealing a story and occasionally too excellent at encouraging one. Table is the numerical cross-check: it shows selected fields as ordered rows, inserts decoded events among them, and follows playback near the same current log time.

steps: Use the inspector to add, remove, and arrange the fields relevant to the hypothesis.
Scrub from Graph or use Table playback to reach the interval.
Read adjacent samples and event rows together; return to Graph for shape and duration.

items: Columns use the same configurable series presentation as Graph, including supported derived fields.
Event rows preserve decoded event order and use available event or main-frame context time.
The view loads a bounded window around the visible time instead of pretending every large log is a tiny spreadsheet.
Displayed values are formatted for their semantic unit. They are not a byte-for-byte raw-frame dump.

blocks.title: Use values to challenge the tuning story

blocks.caption: Useful rows around a suspected event
rows: The requested and measured rates at neighbouring samples.
One sample does not describe latency, damping, or tracking quality.
Which recorded controller contributions were active and how their timing differs.
Term output is not the configured PID or Feedforward gain.
The combined controller demand before motor mixing.
A large value does not identify the term or physical cause responsible.
Whether one or more motor commands approach their available boundary while correction is demanded.
A motor command is not measured RPM, torque, or thrust.
Whether a mode transition, arming state, adjustment, or other event changes the interpretation.
Context time does not create timestamp precision absent from the event payload.

blocks.title: A sample is not the interval between samples
blocks.text: Table can show what was retained at sampled instants. It cannot prove what happened inside a log gap or above the recording's representable frequency range. Pair it with Graph for transient shape, Spectrum for frequency behaviour, and the observed logging rate for evidence limits.

Filter and PID settings are separate configuration evidence. Prefer values written into the selected segment's Blackbox header; use clearly labelled associated configuration only as fallback context. A Table row never silently supplies a missing setting.
